about.title: Exeter Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Exeter is a small, walkable town, but that doesn't mean its stores, sidewalks, and parking areas near Kaweah Street, Palm Avenue, or Visalia Road are free of hazards. A wet floor left unmarked, a cracked walkway, poor lighting in a lot, or an uneven step can cause a serious fall in an instant. California law puts the burden on the injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting what caused your fall and getting surveillance footage preserved before it's erased matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who understands how these claims work in Tulare County and can evaluate what happened to you. Attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Fall in Exeter

items.title: Notice Is Everything in These Cases
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly can mean the difference between having proof of the hazard and having none at all.

items.title: Your Own Actions Can Still Be Weighed
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly, you may still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Exeter?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or park, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: You can still pursue a claim. California's pure comparative fault rule means your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of responsibility, but it doesn't bar you from recovering entirely.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, that's the core of a premises liability claim in California — showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. Photos of the hazard, witness statements, and any available surveillance video from the property can help establish this, which is why acting quickly after a fall in Exeter is important.
